record.paper_title: Some Open Problems in the Theory of Singularities of Mappings
record.context_brief: Alternating homology in corank greater than one
record.original_question: For stable perturbations of map-germs of corank greater than one, how can the alternating homology of their multiple-point spaces D_k(f_t) be calculated, especially when explicit generators are not even known for the defining ideals of D_k(f) for k>2?

evidence.quote: Question 2.4. How to calculate the alternating homology of the multiple point spaces of a stable perturbation for map-germs of corank > 1?
if f has corank > 1, we do not even have explicit generators for the defining ideals of the multiple points spaces Dk(f) for k > 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ be a finitely $\mathcal{A}$-determined holomorphic map-germ of corank greater than one (i.e., $\dim\ker df_0 > 1$), and let $f_t$ be a stable perturbation of $f$. For each integer $k\ge 2$, the $k$-th multiple-point space $D_k(f_t)\subset(\mathbb{C}^n)^k$ is defined as the closure of the set of ordered $k$-tuples of pairwise distinct points mapped to the same image by $f_t$. The symmetric group $S_k$ acts on $D_k(f_t)$ by permuting factors, and the alternating homology $H_*^{\mathrm{Alt}}(D_k(f_t);\mathbb{Q})$ is the subspace of $H_*(D_k(f_t);\mathbb{Q})$ on which $S_k$ acts via the sign representation. This alternating homology is the input of the image-computing spectral sequence converging to the homology of the image (or disentanglement) of $f_t$.

Provide an effective method to compute $H_*^{\mathrm{Alt}}(D_k(f_t);\mathbb{Q})$ for all $k\ge 2$ in the corank $>1$ setting. In particular, since explicit generators for the defining ideals of $D_k(f)$ are not known for $k>2$ when $\mathrm{corank}(f)>1$, determine such generators or otherwise give a procedure that computes the alternating homology of the multiple-point spaces of a stable perturbation without requiring explicit knowledge of these ideals.
artifact.status_search_result: Recent literature on singularities of mappings (e.g., disentanglements of corank-2 map-germs and isotypical components of homology of ICIS) continues to investigate alternating homology of multiple-point spaces, with effective computations available primarily in corank 1 or in isolated corank-2 examples. No general method for computing the alternating homology of multiple-point spaces of stable perturbations of corank >1 map-germs has been established, and defining ideals for $D_k(f)$ with $k>2$ in corank >1 remain unknown in general. The problem appears to remain open.

status_evidence.title: Disentanglements of corank 2 map-germs: two examples
status_evidence.snippet: Mond constructs two examples of finitely determined corank-2 map-germs and computes their disentanglements, illustrating the difficulty of dealing with corank > 1.
status_evidence.claim: Computations in corank >1 remain example-based rather than general.

status_evidence.title: Isotypical components of the homology of ICIS and images of deformations of map germs
status_evidence.snippet: Studies isotypical (including alternating) components of homology of multiple-point spaces using ICIS techniques; results are partial and do not yield a general algorithm for corank >1.
status_evidence.claim: Partial progress on alternating homology but no general method for corank >1.
